issues.failure_explanation: For a general Hurwitz matrix A, the singular values of the Kronecker sum L = I⊗A + A⊗I are not determined by those of A, and sigma_min(L) ≠ 2 sigma_min(A). In fact sigma_min(L) ≤ 2 sigma_min(A) always (apply L to vv^T with v a right singular vector of A for sigma_min(A)), with arbitrarily large gap: for A = [[-1, M],[0, -1]] (Hurwitz), sigma_min(A) ≈ 1/M, while the symmetric residual R = ε e_2 e_2^T yields the symmetric error E = ε[[-M²/8, -M/4],[-M/4, -1/2]], so ||E||_2 ≈ εM²/8 exceeds the certified bound ||R||_F/(2 sigma_min(A)) ≈ εM/2 for M > 4 (with B = I the exact solution X ⪰ 0 and X̃ = X + E ⪰ 0 satisfy all hypotheses of prop1). Even for normal A with eigenvalues -ε ± iω, sigma_min(L) = 2ε but 2 sigma_min(A) = 2√(ε²+ω²). The identity holds only for symmetric negative definite A. Hence prop1's bound, and every bound derived from it, can underestimate the true error by an arbitrarily large factor for the advertised general Hurwitz class.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the constant 2 sigma_min(A) by sigma_min(L) = 1/||L^{-1}||_2 in prop1, teo1, (eq33) and the scaling (eq:52) (prop1's proof already contains the valid bound ||E||_F ≤ ||R||_F/sigma_min(L)), and provide a rigorous computable estimate of sigma_min(L), e.g., by inverse iteration on the Lyapunov operator; for dissipative A (A + A^T ≺ 0) the cheaper denominator 2η with η = -½λ_max(A + A^T) is valid since sigma_min(L) ≥ 2η. Alternatively, restrict all certification statements to symmetric negative definite A, which excludes the paper's own examples.
issues.overall_effect: prop1's error-residual bound is false in general; teo1's certified tolerance (the paper's first main contribution, ||X - X̃||_2 ≤ tol for any prescribed tol) is invalid for non-symmetric A; the practical verification of Assumption ass:statIterGLE via (eq33) and the rescaling strategy of rem:rescaling/(eq:52) can certify ||L^{-1}Π|| < 1 when it actually is ≥ 1, so even the convergence hypothesis of Algorithm 1 can be wrongly confirmed; the choice μ̂ = tol·max_j κ(A_j) in (eqn:cond:LMI) inherits the uncontrolled tolerance; the certification claims in the abstract, the contributions and the conclusions are compromised. The synthetic example of Section 5.1 uses non-normal A_1, A_2 (cf. ISSUE-007), so even the demonstrated certification lies outside the identity's validity class.
issues.title: False identity sigma_min(L)=2 sigma_min(A) invalidates the Lyapunov error-residual bound
issues.why_classification: The first main contribution (certified ||X - X̃||_2 ≤ tol via prop1/teo1) is false as stated for the advertised general Hurwitz class: the certificate can undercut the true error by an arbitrarily large factor, and the same false identity makes the practical check of the standing Assumption ass:statIterGLE and the rescaling justification unsound. The only scope-preserving repair discards the advertised cheap O(n) constant 2 sigma_min(A) and can be arbitrarily conservative for non-normal problems, while the cheap repair (restrict to symmetric A) excludes the paper's own examples and target applications; thus every repair either materially worsens the advertised computability/sharpness of the central guarantee or excludes an advertised regime.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds μ w^T A_j^T w from above by -μ sigma_n(A_j)||w||^2, i.e., it uses w^T A_j^T w ≤ -sigma_n(A_j)||w||^2. But w^T A_j^T w = ½ w^T(A_j + A_j^T)w ≤ ½ λ_max(A_j + A_j^T)||w||^2, so the correct decay rate is η_j := -½λ_max(A_j + A_j^T), which can be arbitrarily smaller than sigma_n(A_j): for normal A_j with eigenvalues -ε ± iω (the very class used in the text to motivate (eqn:ass:ndeAj)), η_j = ε while sigma_n(A_j) = √(ε² + ω²). Hence the stated condition μ ≥ max_j κ(A_j)||X - X̃||_2 does not imply 2 w^T Ê A_j^T w < 0, and the theorem is false as stated. Counterexample satisfying all hypotheses: M = 2, A_1 = [[-0.01, -1],[1, -0.01]], A_2 = [[-0.02, -1],[1, -0.02]] (both normal, Hurwitz, dissipative), N_2 = A_2 - A_1 = -0.01 I, B_1 = B_2 = I; the exact GLE solution X = pI, p ≈ 100.5, satisfies both LMIs (eqn:LMI:P) strictly; κ(A_j) = 1; with X̃ = X + 0.6·diag(1, -1) (so ||X - X̃||_2 = 0.6) and the theorem's choice μ = 0.6, the matrix A_1 X̂ + X̂ A_1^T + B_1 B_1^T for X̂ = X̃ + μI has determinant ≈ -0.40 < 0, i.e., X̂ violates the LMI (eqn:LMI:P).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace sigma_n(A_j) by the dissipativity decay rate η_j = -½λ_max(A_j + A_j^T) in the proof and in (eqn:ass:teo4)/(eqn:cond:LMI), i.e., require μ > max_j (2 sigma_1(A_j)/|λ_max(A_j + A_j^T)|)·||X - X̃||_2 with strict inequality. The theorem's architecture and the synthetic example survive, but the certified perturbation is a different, sometimes much larger, quantity than the advertised tol·κ(A_j).
issues.overall_effect: teo4 (the second main contribution) certifies LMI satisfaction of the perturbed Gramian X̂ = X̃ + μI with a μ that can be arbitrarily too small; consequently the quadratic stability of the resulting ROM (via lemma:qs:MOR) and the applicability of the error bound thm:BTerrorBound to the perturbed Gramians are unjustified whenever η_j < sigma_n(A_j); the recipe μ̂ = tol·max_j κ(A_j) in (eqn:cond:LMI) is not a valid certificate (independently of the tol issue in ISSUE-001); the perturbation-based stability claims in the abstract and conclusions are affected. The numerical validation in Table 1 remains valid only because for those particular matrices η_j ≥ sigma_n(A_j).
issues.title: teo4: invalid inequality w^T A_j^T w ≤ -sigma_n(A_j)||w||^2 makes the certified perturbation mu insufficient
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated (explicit counterexample, already for normal A_j), but a contained repair — a different constant in the μ-condition — restores a recognizably comparable result with the same architecture, and the paper's numerical validation survives; the loss is confined to the size and interpretation of the certified perturbation, not to the method or its scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: with $\fJ_j\in\R^{\stateDim\times\stateDim}$ skew-symmetric, $\fR_j\in\R^{\stateDim\times\stateDim}$ symmetric positive semi-definite, and $\fQ_j\in\R^{\stateDim\times\stateDim}$ symmetric positive definite; cf.~\cite{GilS17}.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the factorization A_j = (J_j - R_j)Q_j with Q_j = I guarantees the strict dissipativity (eqn:ass:ndeAj). With Q_j = I one gets A_j + A_j^T = -2R_j, which is only negative semi-definite because the factorization provides merely R_j ⪰ 0. R_j can be singular while A_j is Hurwitz: e.g., A_j = [[-1, ω],[-ω, 0]] = J_j - R_j with J_j = [[0, ω],[-ω, 0]] skew-symmetric and R_j = diag(1, 0) ⪰ 0 singular; A_j is Hurwitz (its eigenvalues have real part -1/2 for ω ≥ 1/2) but A_j + A_j^T = diag(-2, 0) is not negative definite, so (eqn:ass:ndeAj) fails although Q_j = I. The claim is false as stated; it holds only under the extra condition R_j ≻ 0.

failure_location.quote: Whenever $\fQ_j=\fI_{\stateDim}$ for all $j\in\switchingSet$, it is straightforward to check that \eqref{eqn:ass:ndeAj} is verified.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the condition R_j ≻ 0 (equivalently, state that Q_j = I yields A_j + A_j^T = -2R_j, so that (eqn:ass:ndeAj) holds exactly when R_j is positive definite).
issues.overall_effect: The characterization of the class of switched systems to which teo4 applies is overstated: systems admitting the (J - R) factorization with Q_j = I but singular R_j do not satisfy teo4's hypothesis (eqn:ass:ndeAj), and teo4's proof (which needs w^T A_j^T w < 0 for all w ≠ 0) cannot be applied to them. No labelled result is directly invalidated, since teo4 states (eqn:ass:ndeAj) as an explicit hypothesis.
issues.title: False scope claim: Q_j = I in the factorization (eqn:dH) does not imply strict dissipativity (eqn:ass:ndeAj)
issues.why_classification: A local extra condition (R_j ≻ 0) fully repairs the claim with no effect on any formal result, since teo4 already lists (eqn:ass:ndeAj) as an explicit hypothesis; only the illustrative scope discussion is wrong, and only in the degenerate case of singular R_j.

issues.failure_explanation: In the c-part estimate of the proof (Appendix A-A1), the proof uses X_c(t)^T Σ_{q(t)}^{-2} X_c(t) ≤ σ(q(t))^{-2}||X_c(t)||^2 (valid, since Σ_j ⪰ σ(j)I) and multiplies by λ_1(M_c(q(t))). This multiplication preserves the inequality only when λ_1(M_c) ≥ 0. When λ_1(M_c) < 0 — a generic regime here, since for exactly solved GLEs M_c(j) = -(Σ_i Ň_i Σ_j Ň_i^T + Σ_{i≠j} B̄_i B̄_i^T) ⪯ 0, and the tightening procedure of Section 4.3 (prop5) enforces M_c(j) ⪯ 0 — the step is invalid; a correct argument yields the term σ(q)^2 λ_1(M_c) ∫ X_c^T Σ^{-2} X_c ds (or drops it), which is ≥ λ_1(M_c) ∫ ||X_c||^2 ds. The quantity H_{c,q} in (eq:err:est:2) therefore makes the stated right-hand side strictly smaller than what the proof justifies, and the stated inequality can fail: with K = 0 (no switches), a persistent input, and a truncated σ small enough that |λ_1(M_c)| ∫ ||X_c||^2 ds dominates 4σ² ∫ ||u||^2 ds, the right-hand side of (eq:err:est:2) becomes negative while the left-hand side (∫ ||y - ỹ||^2)^{1/2} is nonnegative.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate teo5 with the positive part λ_1^+(M_c(j)) := max(λ_1(M_c(j)), 0) in the definition of H_{c,q} (or, equivalently, retain the valid term σ(q)^2 λ_1(M_c) ∫ X_c^T Σ_{q}^{-2} X_c ds instead of λ_1(M_c) ∫ ||X_c||^2 ds); the corrected lemma still yields teo6 (together with the sign fix of ISSUE-005).
issues.overall_effect: The single-truncation lemma teo5 is unsupported and can be violated whenever λ_1(M_c(j)) < 0 on some interval — the generic exact-Gramian case and the regime produced by the paper's own LMI-tightening (prop5). teo6, whose proof 'follows directly by applying ... teo5', inherits the gap, although its Heaviside factors already discard negative H-contributions, so teo6's final formula is preserved once teo5 is corrected.
issues.title: teo5: sign-dependent bound on lambda_1(M_c) X_c^T Sigma^{-2} X_c is invalid when lambda_1(M_c) < 0
issues.why_classification: A labelled key lemma is false as stated in a non-degenerate regime that the paper itself targets (M_c ⪯ 0), due to an invalid sign-dependent inference; the repair is a contained weakening of the definition of H_c that preserves the headline theorem teo6, so there is no architectural loss, but the lemma's statement must be genuinely modified rather than typo-fixed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows directly by applying the sub-additivity of the square root function to \Cref{teo5}
As expected, the error bounds lie above the actual errors in all cases.

issues.failure_explanation: teo5 yields err^2 ≤ H_{c,o} - G_{c,o} + 4σ̃²∫||u||^2 per truncation step, so a step with G_{c,o} < 0 worsens the bound by +|G_{c,o}|, and after applying sub-additivity of the square root the correct contribution of that step is +√(|G_{c,o}|)·H(-G_{c,o}) (and 0 when G_{c,o} > 0). In (eq:err:est:3) the third sum is written with a minus sign in front of √(G_{c,o})·H(-G_{c,o}): literally this is not real-valued exactly when the Heaviside factor activates it (G_{c,o} < 0), and under the only sensible reading (√|G_{c,o}|) it enters with the wrong sign, subtracting an adverse contribution that must be added. Hence (eq:err:est:3) can be smaller than the actual output error — it is not a valid bound in the presence of switching-induced jumps with G_{c,o} < 0, which is precisely the regime the term was introduced for (and which is nonzero in the paper's own experiments, cf. the ι-curves in fig5:b). The same wrong sign is used in the experimental estimator ι (eqn:iota) and hence in φ (eqn:err:est:fin). (The second term √(H_{c,o})H(H_{c,o}) has the analogous formal blemish of a square root of a possibly negative number, but there the intended reading is unambiguous and conservative.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the third sum in (eq:err:est:3) by +Σ_k √(-G_{c,o,q}(s_{k+1}, s_k))·H(-G_{c,o,q}(s_{k+1}, s_k)) (equivalently +√|G| for G < 0), and make the same correction in (eqn:iota); the corrected bound is larger, so the reported conclusions that the bounds dominate the actual errors are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's headline error bound teo6 for the PBR method is invalid as written whenever some G_{c,o,q}(s_{k+1}, s_k) < 0: the stated right-hand side can undercut the true output error, so the central guarantee of Section 4 — a generalized error bound accounting for piecewise-constant projection matrices — is not delivered as stated. The defect propagates to the estimator components ι and φ in (eqn:chi)-(eqn:err:est:fin) used in Section 5.2, whose reported bounds are computed with the wrongly signed ι.
issues.title: teo6: wrong sign (and undefined square root) in the G-term makes the PBR error bound able to undercut the true error
issues.why_classification: The stated central guarantee is false (and formally undefined for G < 0) in the regime it targets, which is more than a typo or degenerate-case fix; however the complete repair is a contained sign/absolute-value correction that preserves the bound's three-term structure, its interpretation, and its role in the experiments, so no new architecture or major loss results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the \PBR \ROM $\switchedSysRedJumps$, the dominant contribution to the error bound at higher values of $\stateDimRed$ stems from the violation of the \LMI conditions, i.e., the component $\iota(\stateDimRed, \switchedSysRedJumps)$.
In contrast, we found that this contribution is negligible (around machine precision) for $\switchedSysRedJumpsPert$, and thus we do not display it.

issues.failure_explanation: By the definitions in (eqn:swi:con:fac), the second term of (eq:err:est:3) is built from H_{c,q} and H_{o,q}, i.e., from λ_1(M_c(j)) and λ_1(M_o(j)), the largest eigenvalues of the LMI matrices; it vanishes through the Heaviside factor exactly when the LMIs hold, so it measures inexact LMI satisfaction — not piecewise-constant Gramians. The third term is built from G_{o,q} and G_{c,q}, the jump differences of X_o^T Σ X_o and X_c^T Σ^{-1} X_c at the switching times; it is present even with exact Gramians and is precisely the effect of the piecewise-constant (time-varying) projection matrices — not of inexact LMIs. The prose attributes the two terms to the opposite mechanisms, and the same swap underlies the experimental interpretation in Section 5.2, where the G-component ι (eqn:iota) is identified with 'the violation of the LMI conditions' and claimed to be negligible for the perturbed ROM, although the LMI-enforcing perturbation of Section 4.3 acts on the H-component χ, not on the jump component ι (and fig5:b nonetheless displays ι for the perturbed ROM).

failure_location.quote: the second stems from the use of piecewise constant Gramians in the derivation of \eqref{eqn:new:red:system}; and the third reflects the fact that the numerically computed solutions of the \GLE may not exactly satisfy the \LMI conditions due to approximation errors.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the two attributions (second term ↔ inexact LMIs; third term ↔ piecewise-constant Gramians and state jumps) and correct the corresponding interpretation of χ and ι in Section 5.2.
issues.overall_effect: The interpretation of the paper's main error bound — which mechanism generates which contribution — is misstated, and the attribution of error components in the Black–Scholes experiments (Section 5.2, fig5) is misleading.
issues.title: The roles of the second and third terms of the teo6 bound are swapped in the text
issues.why_classification: The definitions and formulas are unaffected; only the explanatory attribution and the experimental interpretation are wrong, and the repair is a local wording correction with no mathematical loss.

issues.failure_explanation: A_1 is lower bidiagonal with nonzero subdiagonal 1/2; a triangular normal matrix must be diagonal, and indeed (A_1 A_1^T)_{11} = 1 ≠ 1 + 1/4 = (A_1^T A_1)_{11}, so A_1 is not normal. A_2 is tridiagonal Toeplitz with subdiagonal 4/5 and superdiagonal -1/5; normality would require |4/5| = |-1/5|, and indeed (A_2 A_2^T)_{11} = 4 + 1/25 ≠ 4 + 16/25 = (A_2^T A_2)_{11}, so A_2 is not normal either. The stated justification 'normal ⇒ hypothesis of teo4' therefore has a false premise. The conclusion itself — dissipativity (eqn:ass:ndeAj) — survives, since A_j + A_j^T is tridiagonal with negative diagonal and eigenvalues -2 + cos(kπ/(n+1)) resp. -4 + 0.6 cos(kπ/(n+1)), but that direct check is not what the paper states.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, both $\fA_1$ and $\fA_2$ are normal matrices, so the hypothesis of \Cref{teo4} holds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the normality assertion by a direct verification of (eqn:ass:ndeAj), i.e., A_j + A_j^T ≺ 0 for the matrices (eqn:synt:ex) (e.g., via the tridiagonal eigenvalues or Gershgorin's theorem).
issues.overall_effect: The justification given for applying teo4 to the synthetic example is false; the application itself remains valid via direct verification of (eqn:ass:ndeAj). In addition, since A_1 and A_2 are not normal, the example lies outside every class in which the identity sigma_min(L) = 2 sigma_min(A) underlying prop1/teo1 holds (cf. ISSUE-001), so the example does not sit in any regime where the certified bound of Section 3 is known to be valid as stated.
issues.title: False claim that the example matrices A_1 and A_2 are normal
issues.why_classification: The claim is concretely false, but its conclusion survives with an immediate alternative justification, so no result or guarantee is lost; the repair is a short local justification change.
